params.body:
## Why

Since #502, `source_links` and `source_keep` send what Gentells read from each page, so an assistant writes from that and not from the publisher's page. A kept page held only the opening 3,000 characters a post's source is read for, and a signal holds 4,000 at most.

Asked for a paragraph with Eurostat's youth unemployment, an assistant found the Belgian figure missing from what Gentells sent and opened the page itself. That put ec.europa.eu back as a chip beside the text. On that page (euro indicators of 1 October 2026) the figure sits in a country table at character 7,400 of 15,800.

## What

- Keeping a page reads up to 20,000 characters of it (`KEPT_TEXT`) and holds them in a new column, `kept_sources.text`. The signal is left at the 4,000 characters that every reading of signals (classify, the writer, the judge) is sized for.
- `readPage` takes the length as an option. Every other caller keeps the opening of 3,000 as before. A table's cells and rows stay apart (` | `, ` ; `), so a row reads as `Belgium | 18.4 | 19.1 | 19.1`.
- `whatWasRead` takes the kept text when there is one. An answer passes on up to 12,000 characters a page for up to three pages, less when more are named (40,000 in all, as before).
- `bin/reread-kept.mjs` reads the pages kept before this once more, web pages and PDFs, and replaces the kept text only by a longer one. Without `--write` it only says which would change.

## Checked

- `test/kept-sources.test.mjs`: a figure in a table past the opening is kept, its cells apart; the signal stays at 4,000 or less; the reread writes nothing without `--write`, writes the kept text and not the signal with it, and changes nothing a second time.
- The real Eurostat page through the new `readPage`: 15,789 characters, `Belgium | 18.4 | 19.1 | 19.1` at 7,410.
- Full suite 1829 of 1829, `tsc` clean.

## After merge

On the box, once deployed:

```
cd ~/app && node bin/reread-kept.mjs
cd ~/app && node bin/reread-kept.mjs --write
```

The first says which pages get a longer text, the second writes it.
params.title: A kept page holds its whole text, tables included
